subject.title: Add Herdr state bridge for OpenClaw TUI

question: Should Herdr pane-state reporting be a bundled plugin gated by plugin activation, explicit core TUI behavior triggered by Herdr environment, or moved out of core behind a generic TUI status seam?
rationale: The code can be repaired mechanically only after maintainers choose the ownership boundary; the current PR mixes plugin metadata with core env-triggered runtime behavior.

options.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
options.body: Keep the bundled plugin shape, but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin activation honors global disable, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disablement.

options.title: Make It Core-Owned
options.body: Remove the no-op plugin wrapper and document Herdr env-triggered TUI behavior as an explicit core integration, accepting that plugin policy will not control it.

options.title: Move Outside Core
options.body: Pause or close this PR unless a missing generic TUI status extension API is proven, then implement Herdr reporting as an external package.

recommendation.title: Gate Through Plugin Policy
recommendation.body: Keep the bundled plugin shape, but start the sidecar only after resolved plugin activation honors global disable, allowlist, denylist, and per-plugin disablement.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the manifest activation work and has recent TUI/plugin activation history relevant to the boundary choice.
